name: L298N dual H-bridge motor driver module
description: Drives two DC motors from a separate battery. Battery + → 12V, battery − → GND, and also wire GND to the Arduino GND. Motor A on OUT1/OUT2 is controlled by ENA (speed, analogWrite) and IN1/IN2 (direction); motor B on OUT3/OUT4 by ENB and IN3/IN4. The outputs lose about 2 V, so a 6 V pack gives a motor about 4 V.

pins.label: OUT1
pins.description: Motor A terminal 1 (HIGH when IN1 is HIGH and ENA is on).

pins.label: OUT2
pins.description: Motor A terminal 2 (HIGH when IN2 is HIGH and ENA is on).

pins.label: OUT3
pins.description: Motor B terminal 1 (HIGH when IN3 is HIGH and ENB is on).

pins.label: OUT4
pins.description: Motor B terminal 2 (HIGH when IN4 is HIGH and ENB is on).

pins.label: 12V (VS)
pins.description: Motor supply from the battery, 5–35 V (the on-board 5 V regulator needs ≥ 7 V; keep ≤ 12 V with the 5V-EN jumper on).

pins.label: GND
pins.description: Battery − and Arduino GND (all must be common).

pins.label: 5V
pins.description: With the 5V-EN jumper (prop regulatorJumper) this is a 5 V output from the on-board regulator; without it, feed 5 V logic power here.

pins.label: ENA
pins.description: Enable motor A. HIGH = on; analogWrite() here sets motor A's speed. Leave unwired only with the ENA jumper on (prop enaJumper).

pins.label: ENB
pins.description: Enable motor B. HIGH = on; analogWrite() here sets motor B's speed.

props.label: ENA jumper fitted
props.description: Many modules ship with a jumper on ENA tying it HIGH (motor A always enabled, full speed only). Remove it (false) to control speed with analogWrite on ENA.

props.label: 5V-EN jumper fitted
props.description: On-board 78M05 regulator on: the module makes its own 5 V logic supply from 12V (needs ≥ 7 V for a full 5 V) and outputs it on the 5V pin.

footprint: L298N module, 43 × 43 mm, 3 + 2 + 2 screw terminals, 6-pin header

bindings.description: Motor A drive fraction 0..1 (ENA duty × direction inputs).

Motor B summary for the SVG.
